history.heading: Norman island
paragraphs: Jersey, the largest of the Channel Islands, lies about 20 km off the coast of Normandy. It has been inhabited since prehistoric times; La Hougue Bie is a large Neolithic passage grave. The island became part of the Duchy of Normandy in 933 and remained loyal to the English crown when Normandy was lost to France in 1204.
Mont Orgueil Castle was built to defend against French attacks. In 1781 the Battle of Jersey repelled the last French invasion attempt.

history.heading: Occupation
paragraphs: During the Second World War, German forces occupied Jersey from 1940 to 1945, building extensive fortifications, including the Jersey War Tunnels. Liberation Day, 9 May, is the island's national holiday.

culture.heading: Island traditions
paragraphs: English is the main language, and Jèrriais, a form of Norman French, is spoken by a small number of people. Jersey is famous for Jersey cows and their rich milk, Jersey Royal potatoes, and the Battle of Flowers parade. Many place names are French.

politics.heading: Crown Dependency
paragraphs: Jersey is a self-governing British Crown Dependency, not part of the UK or the EU. Its parliament, the States Assembly, makes laws and sets taxes, and a chief minister leads the government. The UK is responsible for defence and international representation.

economy.heading: Finance and agriculture
paragraphs: Financial services, including banking, trusts and fund administration, dominate the economy thanks to low taxes. Tourism and agriculture, including dairy and potatoes, also contribute. The Jersey pound is at par with the British pound.
